pairs.question: Quid ais? Tune me, commilito, spoliare es ausus?
pairs.answer: Sic, imperator, oculi exstillescant mei, si uidi aut tetigi.
pairs.derivation: Pompey (Magnus) interrogates the soldier; speech tag 'Tum Magnus' before and 'Ille continuo exscreat sibi in sinistram et sputum digitis dissipat' (narration) separate it from the reply. Answer is the soldier's oath of denial, stopping at the full stop after 'tetigi'; what follows ('Tum uir animi simplicis...') is narration.

pairs.locus: Phaedrus, Appendix Perottina 11 (Iuno, Venus et gallina)
pairs.question: Dic, sodes, quanto possis satiari cibo?
pairs.answer: Quidquid dederis, satis erit, sic ut concedas pedibus aliquid scalpere.
pairs.derivation: Venus questions the hen (framing 'interrogasse sic gallinam dicitur' dropped before). Answer marked explicitly by 'Respondit illa'; the whole reply is the hen's answer, ending at 'scalpere.'

pairs.locus: Phaedrus, Appendix Perottina 20 (Aesopus et seruus profugus)
pairs.question: Quid tu confusus?
pairs.answer: Dicam tibi clare, pater, hoc namque es dignus appellari nomine, tuto querela quia apud te deponitur.
pairs.derivation: Aesopus asks why the runaway slave is upset. Answer trimmed to the operative opening sentence of the slave's long reply (he will tell Aesopus clearly), ending at the first full stop after 'deponitur'; the rest ('Plagae supersunt...') elaborates his grievances.

pairs.question: Quaeso, bubulce, numquid huc uenit lepus?
pairs.answer: Venit, sed abiit hac ad laeuam,
pairs.derivation: The hunter ('Iamque uenator sequens' narration dropped) asks the herdsman if the hare came by. Answer is the herdsman's deceptive reply, stopping at the full stop; what follows ('et dexteram demonstrat nutu partem') is narration of his contradicting gesture.

pairs.question: Ecquid est gratum tibi, quod te celaui?
pairs.answer: Linguae prorsus non nego habere atque agere maximas me gratias; uerum oculis ut priueris opto perfidis.
pairs.derivation: The herdsman ('Tunc sic bubulcus' framing dropped) asks the hare whether it is grateful that he hid it. The hare answers (thanks to your tongue, but I wish your treacherous eyes blinded); this is the whole reply to the end of the fable.
